transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t stop thinking about how bad I look, especially my face and stomach, and it’s gotten to where I don’t want people to see me anymore. It's really embarrassing to even talk about, but it has gotten to the point where I'm just hiding away.
Have you noticed any changes in your eating habits or weight as a result of these concerns about your appearance?

I haven't really changed my eating habits, and my weight hasn't shifted much. It's just that I can't stop worrying about how saggy and awful my face looks and how much my stomach stands out. I just feel so self-conscious about those areas, regardless of what the scale says.
Do you ever engage in repetitive behaviors, such as excessive mirror checking, grooming, or trying to hide or camouflage the parts of your body that you're concerned about?

Yes, I do, and it's honestly exhausting. I catch myself going to the bathroom mirror every half hour to pull at the skin on my cheeks and poke at my stomach, and I'll change my shirt three times trying to hide my belly. I also constantly ask my wife or daughter if my clothes make me look as bad as I think before I can even bring myself to leave the house.
Can you tell me if your concerns about your face and stomach are related to a fear of gaining weight or if they're more about how your appearance looks to you and others, regardless of your weight?

It’s not really about a fear of gaining weight, but more about how embarrassing and awful my appearance looks to me and everyone else. I just can't stop worrying about my face looking saggy and blotchy and my stomach hanging over my belt, and I constantly picture people staring at these flaws and judging me.
Have you experienced any other distressing thoughts or compulsions beyond your concerns about your appearance, such as obsessive thoughts about germs, order, or safety?
No, I don't have any of those kinds of thoughts or habits about germs, order, or safety. My worries are really just focused entirely on how bad I look.
Can you describe how much time you spend each day thinking about your appearance or engaging in these repetitive behaviors like mirror checking and trying to hide your body parts?

It honestly takes up all day long, with my mind constantly circling back to how bad I look. I find myself checking the mirror every half hour to pull at my cheeks and poke my stomach, and I waste so much time changing shirts and asking my wife for reassurance before I can even think about leaving.
